items.prompt: An object's velocity increases uniformly from $4\text{ m/s}$ to $16\text{ m/s}$ in $6$ seconds. What is its acceleration?
items.explanation: Acceleration is the gradient of a velocity-time graph: $\frac{16-4}{6}=2\text{ m/s}^2$.

items.prompt: A car travels at a constant velocity of $12\text{ m/s}$ for $8$ seconds. How far does it travel?
items.explanation: Distance is the area under the graph. Here it is a rectangle, so the distance is $12\times 8=96\text{ m}$.

items.prompt: A cyclist accelerates uniformly from rest to $20\text{ m/s}$ over $5$ seconds. What distance does the cyclist travel during these $5$ seconds?
items.explanation: The area under the graph is a triangle, so the distance is $\frac{1}{2}\times 5\times 20=50\text{ m}$.

items.prompt: An object's velocity decreases uniformly from $18\text{ m/s}$ to $0\text{ m/s}$ in $3$ seconds. What is its acceleration?
items.explanation: Acceleration is the change in velocity divided by time: $\frac{0-18}{3}=-6\text{ m/s}^2$. The negative sign shows that the object is decelerating.

items.prompt: What does a horizontal line at $-4\text{ m/s}$ on a velocity-time graph represent?

options.text: The object has a constant velocity of $-4\text{ m/s}$
The object has an acceleration of $-4\text{ m/s}^2$

items.explanation: A horizontal line has zero gradient, so the velocity is constant. The negative velocity means the object is moving opposite to the chosen positive direction.
